proposals.name: Understanding the Purpose of Spoken Language
rawLabels: Recognizes that words and sentences help people express ideas

proposals.name: Expressing Needs and Ideas Non-Verbally and Verbally
rawLabels: Uses gestures, actions, facial expressions, or words to communicate ideas and needs

proposals.name: Speaking in Group Settings
rawLabels: Begins to speak appropriately in small and large group interactions

proposals.name: Oral Storytelling
rawLabels: Tells their own stories using words, gestures, and objects

proposals.name: Communicating in Classroom Activities and Play
rawLabels: Uses oral language to communicate during classroom activities, conversations, and imaginative play

proposals.name: Interpreting Visual Information and Media
rawLabels: Attends to visual information showing understanding through discussion, role play and illustrations
Understands that pictures can show feelings and help them understand the story
Explores how pictures and images are made to send messages or feelings
Explores how people learn about the world through what they see, hear, and feel

proposals.name: Using Visual Elements to Share Ideas
rawLabels: Uses colors, shapes, and symbols in drawings and models to share ideas

proposals.name: Inquiring and Questioning Text and Illustrations
rawLabels: Shows curiosity and asks questions about pictures or text

proposals.name: Expressing Opinions About Texts
rawLabels: Expresses opinions about the meaning of a story

proposals.name: Reading and Using Courtesy Words
rawLabels: Reads and uses 10 magic words: please, thank you, sorry, pardon me, excuse me, etc

proposals.name: Writing and Drawing from Personal Experience
rawLabels: Understands that writing helps to share ideas, experiences, and feelings
Uses their own experiences to inspire writing or drawing

proposals.name: Writing Simple Sentences with Sight Words
rawLabels: Writes simple sentences to express ideas
Writes sentences using sight words on their own
Shows simple sentence structure in their writing

rawLabels: Writes phonetically true words, like CVC, CCVC using taught sight words
Writes phonetically true words CCVC (trap), and CVCC (mask), using taught sight words

rawLabels: Use capital letters, full stops in their writing
Uses capital letters, full stops, and question marks in their writing

proposals.name: Identifying Nouns
rawLabels: Identifies nouns as naming words for people, places, animals, and things

proposals.name: Identifying Verbs
rawLabels: Recognizes verbs as action words that show what someone is doing

proposals.name: Using Indefinite Articles (A/An)
rawLabels: Uses the words a and an correctly in simple sentences

proposals.name: Using Demonstrative Pronouns
rawLabels: Uses this and that to talk about things that are near or far
Uses these and those to talk about more than one thing that is near or far

proposals.name: Using Personal Pronouns
rawLabels: Uses he, she, and it to talk about people and things

proposals.name: Comparing and Ordering Quantities and Numbers

Compares and orders sets of objects and numbers up to 50 using appropriate terms such as more, less, and same
Compare and order sets of objects/numbers using appropriate terminology (same, more/less, most/least) up to 99

proposals.name: Sorting Objects into Sets
rawLabels: Sorts objects into sets based on color, shape, and size

proposals.name: Understanding and Using Ordinal Numbers
rawLabels: Uses ordinal numbers to describe the position of objects in a sequence from 1st to 10th and last (oral understanding)
Identify, read, and write ordinal numbers from 1st to 10th

proposals.name: Skip Counting
rawLabels: Perform skip counting in 2's up to 20, and in 5's upto 50 and 10's up to 90

proposals.name: Base-Ten Place Value up to 100

Read, write, and model numbers using the base-10 system up to 99
Recognize the concept of 100 through visual models

rawLabels: Relates addition to combining two groups of objects
Begin to identify pairs of numbers that add up to 10 (number bonds)

rawLabels: Model addition of whole numbers up to 99 without borrowing or carrying over
Perform vertical (for double digit numbers) and horizontal (for single and double digit numbers both) addition
Use strategies such as number lines, counters, number charts to solve addition problems

proposals.name: Subtraction Computation and Strategies
rawLabels: Model subtraction of whole numbers up to 99 without borrowing or carrying over
Perform vertical (for double digit numbers) and horizontal (for single and double digit numbers both) subtraction
Use strategies such as number lines, counters, number charts to solve subtraction problem

proposals.name: Interpreting and Solving Word Problems
rawLabels: Interpret terms like more than, all, both, total, left, take away, minus, less than, and remain in problem situations
Solve simple story sums based on real-life situations

proposals.name: Grouping and Sharing in Equal Sets
rawLabels: Count repeated groups of the same size for groups of 2s and 5s only
Share objects into equal groups and count how many are in each, focusing on groups of 2s and 5s

proposals.name: Identifying Wholes and Halves
rawLabels: Count wholes and halves using groups of objects, such as pizza slices

proposals.name: Identifying and Classifying 2D and 3D Shapes
rawLabels: Identifies 2D shapes by name, such as circle, square, triangle, rectangle
Identify and sort 2D shapes and simple 3D shapes such as cube, cone, cuboid, cylinder, sphere
Classify 2D and 3D shapes based on their properties
Recognize similarities and differences in shapes using terminology such as straight line, curved line, and corner

proposals.name: Composing Shapes and Symmetrical Designs
rawLabels: Make and describe models, shape patterns, and pictures using everyday materials and construction kits
Create symmetrical designs through art

proposals.name: Positional and Directional Language
rawLabels: Use everyday language to describe position, direction, and movement (e.g., next to, beside, in front of, behind, over, under, inside, outside, above, below, left, and right)

proposals.name: Direct and Non-Standard Measurement
rawLabels: Tell which object has more or less.
Measure objects using non-standard tools like handspan, footspan, or blocks.
Compare the lengths of two or more objects.
Use simple tools (hands, clocks, calendars) to find out measurements.

proposals.name: Time and Calendar Concepts
rawLabels: Read time to the hour on an analogue clock (o'clock).
Name the days of the week and months of the year.
Use a calendar to find the date and talk about special days.

proposals.name: Coins, Currency, and Value
rawLabels: Identify and recognize basic coins and notes (1, 2, 5, 10, 20) used in their country.
Understand that money is used to buy things.

proposals.name: Identifying, Describing, and Extending Patterns
rawLabels: Identify repeated and growing patterns (arranged in increasing order)
Describe and extend patterns involving colour, shape, size, things around them, and numbers

Describe patterns found in nature
Recognize and describe number patterns using skip counting (e.g., by 2s, 5s, and 10s)

proposals.name: Inverse Relationship of Addition and Subtraction
rawLabels: Begin to understand the inverse relationship between simple addition and subtraction using concrete and pictorial support

proposals.name: Collecting, Sorting, and Graphing Data
rawLabels: Sort objects into groups in different ways and explains how they are sorted.
Count and collects data by looking around and asking questions.
Show data using pictures and simple bar graphs.
Answer questions by looking at simple graphs.

proposals.name: Language of Chance and Probability
rawLabels: Talk about chances of something happening, like maybe or not possible.
Notices and talks about changes in daily events using words like maybe, less likely, or certain.

proposals.name: Expressing Ideas and Needs in Hindi
rawLabels: Use gestures, actions, body language and/or words to communicate needs and to express ideas

proposals.name: Listening to Stories, Poems, and Songs in Hindi
rawLabels: Join in with poems, rhymes and songs

proposals.name: Visual Comprehension and Response in Hindi

Use body language to communicate and to convey understanding, for example, pointing, gesturing, facial expressions.
Listen to terminology associated with visual texts and understand terms such as colour, shape, size.

proposals.name: Letter Formation, Directionality, and Spacing in Hindi
rawLabels: Experiment with writing using different writing implements and media.
Forming letters and words on paper.
Understands that it's important to space between two letters and words.
Understand how to write, like where letters start, space between them, and how to write from left to right.

proposals.name: Visual Arts Exploration and Material Selection
rawLabels: Engage with and enjoy a variety of visual arts experiences
Select tools, materials and processes for specific purposes
Take responsibility for the care of tools and materials
Participate in individual and collaborative creative experiences
Create artwork in response to a range of stimuli

proposals.name: Responding to and Analyzing Artworks
rawLabels: Enjoy experiencing artworks
Describe what they notice about an artwork
Identify the materials and processes used in the creation of an artwork
Communicate their initial responses to an artwork in visual, oral or physical modes
Make personal connections to artworks

proposals.name: Exploring Vocal and Instrumental Sounds
rawLabels: Explore a range of vocal sounds, rhythms, instruments and timbres to communicate ideas and feelings
Explore body and untuned percussion instrument sounds

proposals.name: Movement, Tempo, and Physical Coordination
rawLabels: Create movement to various tempos
Develop physical balance and coordination
Respond to word, rhythm and/or music through movements.

Display audience etiquette and appropriate responses such as watching, listening and responding to favourite parts of the performance.

rawLabels: Show curiosity about live and recorded dance performances
Move their bodies to express the mood of the music
Express their responses to music in multiple ways (drawings, games, songs, dance, oral discussion).
Describe how music makes them feel
Identify the rhythmic patterns.
